text.headline: Timeline of Maldives
text.text: Major events in the history of Maldives.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The Maldives is believed to have been settled by Dravidian peoples from the Indian subcontinent around 3000 BCE. These early inhabitants established fishing and agricultural communities on the islands.

events.headline: Conversion to Islam
events.text: The Maldives officially converted to Islam in 1153 AD under the influence of a Moroccan traveler, Abu al-Barakat. This marked a significant cultural and religious shift for the islands.

events.headline: Portuguese Colonization
events.text: The Portuguese established control over the Maldives in 1558, leading to a period of foreign domination. Their presence was met with resistance from the local population.

events.headline: End of Portuguese Rule
events.text: The Maldives expelled the Portuguese in 1573 after a successful uprising led by Muhammad Thakurufaanu Al-Azam. This event is celebrated as a national holiday in the Maldives.

events.headline: British Protectorate
events.text: The Maldives became a British protectorate in 1887, which lasted until the mid-20th century. This arrangement allowed the British to control foreign affairs while the local sultan retained internal authority.

events.headline: First Constitution
events.text: The Maldives adopted its first constitution in 1932, marking a shift towards modern governance. This document established a parliamentary system and limited the powers of the sultan.

events.headline: First Republic
events.text: The Maldives declared itself a republic for the first time in 1953, abolishing the monarchy. However, this republic was short-lived and the sultanate was restored later that year.

events.headline: Independence from Britain
events.text: The Maldives gained full independence from British rule on July 26, 1965. This marked a new era of self-governance and national identity for the islands.

events.headline: Second Republic
events.text: The Maldives established its Second Republic in 1968 after a coup that deposed the last sultan, Muhammad Fareed Didi. This led to the establishment of a presidential system.

events.headline: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom's Presidency
events.text: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom became president in 1978, serving for 30 years. His administration was marked by economic development but also by authoritarian practices.

events.headline: 2004 Tsunami
events.text: The Maldives was severely affected by the Indian Ocean tsunami on December 26, 2004, which caused extensive damage and loss of life. The disaster prompted international aid and reconstruction efforts.

events.headline: New Constitution
events.text: A new constitution was adopted in 2008, establishing a multi-party democracy and enhancing civil liberties. This marked a significant political transition for the Maldives.

events.headline: First Democratic Elections
events.text: The first democratic presidential elections were held in the Maldives in 2008, leading to the election of Mohamed Nasheed. This was a historic moment for the country's political landscape.

events.headline: Nasheed's Resignation
events.text: President Mohamed Nasheed resigned on February 7, 2012, amid political turmoil and protests. His resignation was controversial and led to debates about the legitimacy of the transition.

events.headline: Presidential Elections
events.text: Presidential elections were held in September 2013, resulting in the election of Abdulla Yameen. His presidency was marked by political unrest and allegations of authoritarianism.

events.headline: Political Crisis
events.text: The Maldives faced a political crisis in 2015, with increasing tensions between the government and opposition. This culminated in protests and calls for democratic reforms.

events.headline: Election of Ibrahim Mohamed Solih
events.text: Ibrahim Mohamed Solih was elected president in September 2018, marking a significant political shift. His administration promised to restore democracy and address human rights issues.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The Maldives faced the COVID-19 pandemic starting in March 2020, which significantly impacted its tourism-dependent economy. The government implemented various measures to control the spread of the virus.

events.headline: Continued Political Developments
events.text: As of 2023, the Maldives continues to navigate political challenges and economic recovery post-pandemic. The government is focusing on enhancing tourism and addressing climate change issues.
